images.title: Which jump lands on both?
images.purpose: Show that a jump size lands on a treasure only when it is a factor of it, comparing jumps of 4 and of 6 for treasures on 12 and 18.
images.composition: Two number lines from 0 to 18 stacked one above the other across the frame, white space between and around them.
exact_structure: Each number line runs from 0 to 18 with small grey (#6B7280) ticks at every whole number; only 0, 12 and 18 are labelled with numbers.
On both lines, reddish purple (#CC79A7) treasure chests sit above 12 and above 18.

Top line: exactly 4 teal (#0072B2) arcs of length 4 from 0 to 4, 4 to 8, 8 to 12, 12 to 16, labelled jump of 4; a green (#009E73) tick at the chest on 12 and a vermilion (#D55E00) cross at the chest on 18.
Bottom line: exactly 3 amber (#E69F00) arcs of length 6 from 0 to 6, 6 to 12, 12 to 18, labelled jump of 6; green (#009E73) ticks at both chests.
rejection: any count of arcs other than 4 on the top line and 3 on the bottom line
an arc of 4 drawn landing on 18
chests placed anywhere other than 12 and 18
images.takeaway: A jump lands on both treasures only when its size is a common factor of both numbers.
images.description: Two number lines to 18: jumps of 4 land on 12 but miss 18, while jumps of 6 land on both 12 and 18.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask why 4 misses 18; link landing to dividing exactly.

image_decisions.why: The jump game is a number line idea, so a number line picture carries the mathematics.
